llm.reasoning: The anomalous month (2026-02) has penalty_total_brl=0, which is a severe drop from the median of previous 12 months (30.5M). Seasonality check shows the calendar month 2 (February) deviated below 1 in 2 of 6 years (2021-02: 0.93, 2023-02: 0.57), but the same month was not flagged in other years. The data quality indicators (excluded, no_id) are 0, so no reporting failure. No known events. The Page-Hinkley test shows no sustained level shift. The penalty value of 0 is implausible for an active series (expected 30.5M). This suggests a data-quality event (e.g., retroactive correction or system migration) causing the zero value.

The anomalous month (2025-07) has penalty_total_brl = 0, which is implausible for an active series. Seasonality check shows the same month (Jul) deviated below 1 in 3 of 6 years (2022-2024), but the 2025-07 value is 0, while previous years had ratios >0.19. No known events in +-6 months. The data shows no excluded or no_id records, but the value is implausibly low (zero) in a series where monthly penalties are typically millions. A Page-Hinkley test found no sustained level shift. This is a data-quality event (DQE) as the value is implausible, likely a reporting failure or system error.

The data shows no excluded records or records without identifier (no_id=0) and plausible values (no zeros in other months except Jan 2025). The anomaly is a single month with 0 notices, while previous months had active enforcement (e.g., 195 in Nov 2024). A data-quality event would require a burst of excluded records or no_id records, but these are 0. The sustained level shift test is negative. Thus, the anomaly is likely a genuine enforcement shift (GES), as it's a real drop with no seasonal pattern or data issue evidence.

Value 0 is implausible (penalty_total_brl was active in prior months). The anomaly is a sustained zero, which is likely a data-quality issue (e.g., system error causing no records to be reported).

Since seasonality is weak (only 1 year with similar deviation) and no policy events, the anomaly likely stems from a data-quality issue (e.g., retroactive correction or system migration) despite the large deviation.

Seasonality check shows 2023-11 ratio 0.15 (low), 2022-11 0.94 (near median), 2021-11 2.29 (high), 2020-11 0.10 (low), 2019-11 1.50 (high). Only 2022 and 2021 had ratios above 1 (high) for Nov, while 2024-11 is 39x median. But the same calendar month deviated in the same direction (above 1) in 2 of 5 years, so seasonal pattern exists. However, the 2024-11 value is unusually high (195 vs median 5) and the same month wasn't flagged in other years. The anomaly is flagged by multiple detectors (zscore, mad, iforest) but Page-Hinkley test shows no sustained level shift. No data quality indicators (excluded/no_id records) are present. The high value could be a genuine enforcement shift (GES) as no policy events, seasonal pattern, or data issues are evident.

Seasonality check shows 2023-07, 2022-07, 2021-07, 2020-07 had ratios >1, but 2024-07 is 0.00 (40k vs 22.6M median). Only 2 of 5 years had same downward deviation. 2025-07 also flagged (0 penalty). No known events. Records show no excluded/no_id records; penalty value is implausibly low (40k vs typical millions). No sustained shift. Data quality event fits: zero penalty with no identifier, unlikely to be genuine enforcement. Confidence: 0.95

The anomaly is in 2023-12 with penalty_total_brl = 0, while the median of previous 12 months was 21.2M. Seasonality check shows 2022-12: 0.04, 2021-12: 1.62, 2020-12: 0.02, 2019-12: 3.48. The same calendar month deviated below 1 in 2 of 4 years (2020-12, 2022-12), but no other year was flagged. No known policy events. Records show no excluded or no_id entries, no data quality issues. The zero value is implausible for an active series (all prior months had positive penalties). This suggests a data problem: likely a system error or retroactive correction that caused the month to have no penalties. The Page-Hinkley test shows no sustained level shift, ruling out genuine enforcement shifts.

Seasonality check shows 2023-05 had a ratio of 0.01 (vs median 44.7M), while previous years had ratios 3.29 (2022-05), 1.97 (2021-05), 0.59 (2020-05). Only 1 of 3 years had a below-1 deviation, so not strong seasonal pattern. No other years had this month flagged as anomalous. Known event: 2023-01 political change (policy-driven). But data shows no excluded/no_id records (0), no implausible values (399k is plausible for 5 notices), and no sustained shift. Since no data quality issues, and event is policy-driven, but the anomaly is a single month with very low penalties (399k vs 44.7M median), likely a data error (e.g., misreported value) rather than genuine shift. No other data issues, so DQE most plausible.

Seasonality check shows 2021-09: 1.17 (above median), 2020-09: 0.35 (below), 2019-09: 2.33 (above). The same calendar month deviated above median in 2 of 3 years (2019, 2021), but not in 2020. However, no other year had this month flagged as anomalous. The spike in 2022-09 (68 notices vs. median 6) is unusually high but not explained by prior seasonal patterns. No data quality issues (excluded/no_id records = 0) and no policy events within 6 months except a political change in 2023-01 (4 months later), too late to impact 2022-09. The Page-Hinkley test shows no sustained shift. Thus, the anomaly is likely a genuine enforcement shift (GES).

pt.Seasonality check shows 2021-09: 1.17 (a: Verificação de estação mostra 2021-09: 1,17 (acima da mediana), 2020-09: 0,35 (abaixo), 2019-09: 2,33 (acima). O mesmo mês se desviou acima da mediana em 2 de 3 anos (2019, 2021), mas não em 2020. No entanto, nenhum outro ano teve este mês marcado como anômalo. O pico em 2022-09 (68 notificações vs. mediana 6) é muito alto, mas não explicado por padrões sazonais anteriores. Não há problemas de qualidade de dados (registros excluídos/não_id = 0) e nenhum evento político dentro de 6 meses, exceto uma mudança política em 2023-01 (4 meses depois), o que foi tarde demais para impactar o 2022-09. O teste Page-Hinkley mostra sem deslocamento sustentado. Assim, a anômalia é provavelmente um deslocamento genuíno de enforcement (GES).
Verificação de sazonalidade mostra que a razão de 2023-11 é 0,15 (baixa), 2022-11 é 0,94 (próxima da mediana), 2021-11 é 2,29 (alta), 2020-11 é 0,10 (baixa) e 2019-11 é 1,50 (alta). Apenas 2022 e 2021 tiveram razões acima de 1 (alta) em novembro, enquanto 2024-11 é 39x a mediana. No entanto, o mesmo mês se desviou na mesma direção (acima de 1) em 2 de 5 anos, portanto, existe um padrão sazonal. No entanto, o valor de 2024-11 é extremamente alto (195 vs mediana 5) e o mesmo mês não foi marcado em outros anos. A anomalia é detectada por múltiplos detectores (zscore, mad, iforest), mas o teste Page-Hinkley não mostra deslocamento de nível sustentado. Não há indicadores de qualidade de dados (registros excluídos/não_id) presentes. O valor alto pode ser uma mudança genuína de enforcement (GES) já que não há eventos políticos, padrão sazonal ou problemas de dados evidentes.
